To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of standard very deep submicron CMOS process on high-resistivity wafers is a very attractive option for the realization of monolithic detectors for high energy physics.
a uniform depletion depth of 40 μm can be obtained by reverse biasing the device with 100 V and that the signal-to-noise ratio of a 100 μm thick sensor is 10.5.
the use of standard deep-submicrons CMOS technologies for monolithic sensors is feasible and that the proposed sensor concept offers an interesting alternative to hybrid pixel detectors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new type of monolithic detectors that combine the advantages of hybrid and monolithic detectors.
the development of a new class of monolithic detectors that can be fabricated using the same CMOS process used for the fabrication of standard CMOS integrated circuits.
the feasibility study of a novel monolithic sensor for particle tracking based on a 0.13-μm CMOS technology with 40-μm-thick high resistivity silicon substrate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed concept is very promising for the realization of low power and low material budget detectors that are suitable to be integrated in a monolithic way in standard very deep submicron CMOS technologies.
the use of a standard deep-submicrom CMOS technology with a resistivity of 100 Ω· cm is not adequate to implement a monolithic pixel detector for particle tracking.

a monolithic pixel detector based on a standard CMOS process can be designed and implemented, and that it is possible to obtain the desired performance, in particular a high charge collection efficiency, a low noise and a low power consumption, even with a large depletion thickness.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a 40 μm thick fully depleted detector can be realized in a standard 0.18 μm CMOS process with an area of 100 μm × 100 μm, a leakage current below 1 nA and a capacitance of about 1 pF.
